newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-INTERVIEW-PMP says outlook is better.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-INTERVIEW-PMP says outlook is better.

text.p: Magazine publisher PMP Communications Ltd said on Thursday it expected full year profits to be boosted by a strong second half underpinned by recovering circulation, advertising revenues and lower costs.

"There are signs that the second half will be better than the last half of last year...We're still trying to better last year's result and at this stage we think that's achievable," managing director Ken Catlow told Reuters in an interview.
Catlow said advertising revenues were set to recover but growth was coming mainly from successful small to medium-sized businesses.

"The larger (businesses) are tightening their purse strings. The smaller ones are saying: "We are where we are. It's a bit like it's raining. There's not much you can do about it so let's go out and create some interest in our product," he said.
Catlow said catalogue publishing remained tough in the early part of the second half but magazine circulation was strengthening on the back of new publications.
"'That's Life' continues to go from strength to strength. The European publications are going very well and the youth publications are doing very well," he said.
Circulation also had improved for PMP's flagship women's magazine New Idea, he added.
PMP, formed in 1991 when News Corp's Australian unit spun off its publishing and commercial printing operations, posted a 1995/96 net profit of A$58.04 million.
Catlow the magazine division had pinned its future on new publications.
"If we hadn't done that with 'That's Life' we wouldn't be selling the sort of magazine numbers we are today. We think we've found a few new niches in the market."
With the integration of multi-media business Shomega complete, PMP would ramp up its use of digital technology, Catlow said.

"Digital photography is coming in very strongly now. That eliminates scanning of film completely and our first digital plate makers will be in about April-May of this year which means we can take it all the way from a camera to a printing press without touching it," he said.
Catlow said Shomega, which PMP bought for about A$176 million in June last year, would capitalise on strong growth in the CD-ROM market and steady demand for audio compact disks.
He said PMP also would be Australia's first manufacturer of digital video disks (DVD) which are tipped to replace the current CD-ROM format.
